root_cause:
In Console.print, when soft_wrap=True and a style is given, the rendered segments (which include the trailing '
' Segment emitted by Text's end='
') are passed whole through Segment.apply_style(..., self.get_style(style)) and appended straight to the buffer. The newline segment therefore gets the style, so the output is '\x1b[34;47mtext\x1b[0m\x1b[34;47m
\x1b[0m' and the background bleeds onto the next terminal line when it scrolls. The soft_wrap=False path never had this because it runs Segment.split_and_crop_lines, which strips newlines and re-adds an unstyled Segment.line().
best_solution: Add a classmethod Segment.split_lines_terminator(segments) -> Iterable[Tuple[List[Segment], bool]] that splits on '\n' in non-control segments like split_lines, but yields (line, True) for every line that ended in a newline and (line, False) for a trailing partial line. In Console.print's styled branch, compute render_style = self.get_style(style) once, and for each renderable iterate `for line, add_new_line in Segment.split_lines_terminator(render(renderable, render_options))`: extend(Segment.apply_style(line, render_style)) and, if add_new_line, append an unstyled Segment.line(). The style is applied only to line content and the newline is emitted bare, so the reset lands before '\n'. No padding, no cropping, so soft-wrap semantics are untouched.
acceptable_alternatives: Behaviorally, any change that applies the print style only to non-newline segments in the soft_wrap path (e.g. splitting with the existing Segment.split_lines and re-joining with unstyled Segment.line(), careful to preserve whether the last line had a terminator) fixes test_soft_wrap_styled. It would still fail 2 of the 3 hidden tests, which call Segment.split_lines_terminator by name and check its exact (list, bool) tuple output.
hidden_test_demands:
tests/test_segment.py::test_split_lines_terminator: list(Segment.split_lines_terminator([Segment('Hello
World')])) == [([Segment('Hello')], True), ([Segment('World')], False)]. tests/test_segment.py::test_split_lines_terminator_single_line: [Segment('Hello')] -> [([Segment('Hello')], False)]. tests/test_text.py::test_soft_wrap_styled: Console(color_system='standard', width=80, force_terminal=True); print('soft wrap is on', style='blue on white', soft_wrap=True) then print('Next line') must capture exactly '\x1b[34;47msoft wrap is on\x1b[0m
Next line
'. Existing tests/test_text.py::test_soft_wrap (expects '\x1b[37;44m Hello World \x1b[0m
', no padding) must keep passing.
locating_signals: Statement is only the PR title 'fix background style with soft wrap' plus an issue link; the agent never sees the issue text or the repro. 'soft wrap' leads to the soft_wrap handling in Console.print (rich/console.py), where the styled branch calls Segment.apply_style over whole renders. No function is named, and the new API Segment.split_lines_terminator is not mentioned anywhere in the statement.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4: no source change at all, only two scratch files (reproduce_issue.py, test_soft_wrap_fix.py); the agent comments show it guessed the bug was about terminal wrap and never found the styled-newline cause. v6: added an elif soft_wrap branch running split_and_crop_lines(..., pad=True), which pads every soft-wrapped line to console width with spaces; this broke the existing test_soft_wrap and test_soft_wrap_styled (trailing spaces before '\n'). v7: same idea with width=10**9 plus manual padding to self.width using the last segment's style; broke test_soft_wrap and put the padding after the newline. v8: empty patch after 180 s / 79 calls. No config added Segment.split_lines_terminator, so the two segment tests failed with AttributeError in every run; even a correct behavioral fix would have scored 1/3.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is just a bug-title plus an issue link, first reproduce the exact byte output (print repr of captured ANSI output with force_terminal) and diff the failing path against the sibling path that works (here soft_wrap=False vs True); the fix usually makes the broken path mirror the working one. Never 'fix' rendering by padding or adding characters: existing tests pin exact output strings. And because hidden tests from maintainer PRs often unit-test a small new helper, factor the core logic into a well-named helper on the class that already owns similar helpers (split_lines -> split_lines_<variant>), following that family's naming and return conventions.
